rv.q: “North by Northwest” showcases what happens when talented artists take a familiar story and joyfully reinvent it.
Even with those pacing issues, the lighthearted thriller still succeeds as retro summer escapist fun.
What keeps this production at arm's length is its insistence on explaining its own cleverness.

Kudos to Etta Murfitt, who choreographed this piece, creating exciting, complex, unexpected, and seamless movements for the performers that suggest their long-distance journeys and the duration of each event.

cn.t: Emma Rice's adaptation succeeds with style and panache, transforming Hitchcock's thriller into inventive physical theatre. Critics praise the creative staging and meta-theatrical approach, though the beloved film remains the benchmark.
